id: # First life after the tutorial: show them what survived them.

speaker: cousin
text: Your cousin found your sparking rocks. He wants to know how they work.
notes: Inherited-answer callback: almost always the first card of life 2.

speaker: cousin
text: Your cousin keeps a pile of dry grass by the fire. For sitting.

speaker: elder
text: It's raining again. Everything we own is wet, including the fire.

speaker: cousin
text: Your cousin says sleeping on a flat rock is great for your back.
notes: Feeds the rock pillow bad idea.

speaker: cousin
text: Your cousin fell asleep on his dry grass pile, right next to your sparks.

speaker: elder
text: The elder's story about the big fish gets bigger every night.

speaker: cousin
text: Your cousin scratches a line on the wall every time the moon comes back.

speaker: cousin
text: The hunters keep arguing about where the mammoths go. Nobody can remember.

speaker: kid
text: A kid named a rock and takes it everywhere. Now all the kids want one.
notes: Feeds the pet rock bad idea.

speaker: kid
text: A kid drew a mammoth on the cave wall. The legs are all wrong.
epitaph: Invented art, by accident, while scolding a child.
notes: The matching answer is the scolding one.

id: # Leanings toward fire (the keystone needs sparks and tinder first)

speaker: elder
text: Someone has to stay up all night and feed the fire. The elders nominate you.

speaker: shaman
text: Lightning hit the big tree. The shaman says the Gods are handing out fire.

speaker: cousin
text: A wolf is sniffing around the babies again.

speaker: neighbours
text: The tribe across the river has fire whenever they want. They're smug about it.

speaker: neighbours
text: The tribe across the river wants its fire back. They've brought rocks.

speaker: elder
text: The elder will protect your fire from the Gods. For a small fee, in meat.
notes: Feeds the fire insurance bad idea.

speaker: elder
text: The fire's out again. Everyone's looking at you, your sparks, and that dry grass.
right effects: use sparks; use tinder; Fire +25; Tribe +10

speaker: shaman
text: The Gods demand the sparkly rock.

speaker: shaman
text: The shaman says if we dance hard enough, it will rain meat.

speaker: shaman
text: The volcano rumbled. The shaman says it wants a snack.

speaker: cousin
text: Found red berries. Nobody has tried them yet.

speaker: elder
text: The cave is crowded. Someone suggests a second cave.

speaker: cousin
text: Your cousin tied a pointy rock to a stick. He's very pleased with himself.

speaker: cousin
text: A mammoth wandered into the valley. The hunters want to try something bold.

speaker: mammoths
text: The mammoth didn't enjoy that. It's back, with friends.

speaker: mammoths
text: The herd is circling the cave. Someone has to distract them.
right effects: use sparks; Fire -10; Gods +10; firemaking +2; next sa-stampede-3

speaker: mammoths
text: It's over. The herd left, with half the food and most of your cousin.

speaker: mother
text: Are you eating? You look like a stick with hair.

speaker: mother
text: When are you going to settle down in a nice cave of your own?

speaker: mother
text: These sparks. Is that a real job?

speaker: naysayer
text: Sparks. Great. Now nobody in this tribe has eyebrows.

speaker: naysayer
text: Pictures on the wall? It'll never catch on.

speaker: naysayer
text: You're cooking the meat again. My father ate it cold, and he lived to nearly twenty.

speaker: animal
notes: A card with no text, just an animal. Something happens. Never explained.

speaker: advisor
text: Don't do the thing with the... ah, do it. It's funnier. I'll see you when someone writes something down.
notes: Appointment 1 of 3. He returns in the Bronze Age once writing exists.

speaker: elder
text: The tinder pile is the comfiest thing we own. People keep napping on it.

speaker: cousin
text: The hunters want the mammoth drawing moved nearer the exit, for luck.

speaker: mother
text: Take your grandfather's rock pillow. Your neck needs it.

speaker: kid
text: The pet rock ran away. Nobody can explain how.

speaker: elder
text: The fire went out. Your fire insurance says that was an act of the Gods.

id: # After this life's breakthrough (it goes on; points stop counting)

speaker: cousin
text: Now that dry grass catches sparks, nobody wants to sleep on it. Except your cousin.

speaker: kid
text: Everyone wants their face on the cave wall now. The wall is full.

speaker: elder
text: Now that anyone can make fire, the old fire keeper wants a new job.

id: # Fame: high-stakes cards once you've invented something this life (the consequences arrive)

speaker: cousin
text: Everyone's copying your invention. Badly. Two huts are on fire.

speaker: shaman
text: The shaman says your invention came from the Gods, and the Gods want credit.

speaker: elder
text: People walk for days to see you. They're eating all the food.

speaker: neighbours
text: The tribe across the river says they invented it first. They brought a rock to prove it.

id: # Fallback when the deck runs dry (should be rare; the checker and bot watch for it)

speaker: narrator
text: Nothing happens today. The tribe looks at you, expecting something.
